maria: Heads up — saw a regression on canary this morning where the FP8 path is consistently slower than INT8 for our mixed-length chat workload. attaching quick profiler snapshot

maria: ```
profile summary (per-request wall): 120.4 ms
  runtime/fp8_kernel            52.1 ms  (43.3%)
  runtime/kv_slice_copy         28.4 ms  (23.6%)
  batching/align_and_pad        20.3 ms  (16.9%)
  runtime/int8_kernel           10.2 ms  (8.5%)
  other                         9.4 ms   (7.8%)
```

maria: Repro: ./bin/bench --model gptx-small --batcher continuous --seq-lens 8,32,128 --quant fp8_mixed --iters 500

kevin: Is that coming from the continuous-batcher coalescing different quant shapes?

maria: Yes — the continuous batcher groups the short+long sequences. When those merge, we see an extra memcopy in the KV path (the kv_slice_copy line above). The copy is only present on the FP8 kernel code path.

anika: Can you paste the nvprof / telemetry flame output for the long request? even a few kernel lines helps.

maria: ```
flame (top kernels):
  kernel_fp8_matmul            45.2%
  kernel_fp8_pack              12.8%
  kv_slice_copy                23.6%   <-- host memcpy triggered by misaligned slice
  kernel_int8_matmul            8.5%
  batch_align_pad               9.9%
```

ryan: That smells like alignment aliasing. Our FP8 microkernels assume 32-byte-aligned KV bases and contiguous strides. If a slice base isn't 32-aligned we fallback to a generic code-path that does an intermediate pack (hence the memcpy). Batcher pads currently to multiples of 8 tokens which doesn't guarantee the byte alignment required by FP8 packing.

kevin: So when a short sequence (8 tokens) is packed next to a long one (128) the resulting slab layout can produce unaligned offsets for the later slice?

maria: Exactly. The allocator returns 8-byte aligned slabs in most cases; FP8 pack expects 32. When mixed shapes are interleaved the slice_base % 32 != 0 and we hit the fallback. The fallback memcopy costs more than the FP8 kernel speedup, so overall FP8 is slower than INT8 here.

anika: Two levers: (A) change batcher padding/alignment strategy (pad to 32-byte alignment or token multiple that maps to 32 bytes), (B) add fast-path that remaps misaligned slices to a temporary 32-aligned buffer only when beneficial, (C) prefer INT8 kernel when alignment mismatch detected.

ryan: I sketched numbers locally. Cheap heuristic: if fallback copy > 12% of request, prefer int8. Remap threshold helps but adds memcpy overhead and complexity for KV cache eviction.

maria: Also want telemetry for: alignment_mismatch_count, remap_bytes, chosen_kernel (fp8|int8|remap). We need a signal before enabling FP8 widely.

kevin: For quick mitigation, we can: (1) modify continuous-batcher padding to pad incoming sequences to token multiples that guarantee 32-byte alignment for the quant layout (LCM of token-size alignment), (2) add a canary gate to disable FP8 for continuous-batcher until fixed.

perf-bot: Created PERF-9742: "FP8 alignment aliasing causing KV memcopy in continuous-batcher" and attached the profiler snapshot.

deploy-bot: Temporarily disabled FP8-mixed quant canary in region us-west-2 for 2 hours.

maria: Thanks. Proposed plan: Ryan to prototype alignment-guard + unit tests (ensures slice_base % 32 == 0 or routes to int8), Anika to add telemetry metrics, Kevin to update batcher pad heuristic, I'll coordinate canary and perf checks.

ryan: I'll start a branch: runtime/kv/alignment-guard. Plan: add align_check() in kv_slice_viewer, unit test with random slab layouts, fallback policy toggle via runtime flag. ETA: EOD tomorrow for prototype.

kevin: I'll prepare a small change to continuous-batcher to pad to 16-token multiples first (low risk) and then adjust to force 32-byte alignment if prototype looks good.

anika: I'll add telemetry fields to the perf schema and a quick dashboard: alignment_mismatch / request_count, remap_bytes / day. Will post dashboard link in the thread when ready.

maria: Nice. Also please add an integration test that runs bench with seq-lens mix and asserts no fallback memcopy on FP8 path (or that fp8 is still net-wins).

ryan: Will do. tagging @kevin for rollout approvals.

maria: Thanks all — appreciate the fast triage. :thumbsup:
